findings.title: Autopilot run from a holdout-folder kit copy hashes the repo's kit tree, not the code that is running
findings.problem: The module comment (lines ~77-80) says the autopilot can run from a holdout folder's kit copy. In that case freeze_check is loaded from --repo, and verify(manifest, 'holdout-autopilot', repo=repo) runs _check_kit_tree. That check hashes <repo>/docs/design/holdout-v2.12/tools (KIT_KEYS -> fm.HOLDOUT_KIT_PREFIX under live['repo']), never the copy that is executing. A changed or stale kit copy in the folder therefore passes the identity check while the repo tree matches. The README binding table says the autopilot is bound by 'kit tree hash'. pending: confirm that sealing sessions really run from the folder copy rather than the repo checkout.
findings.fix_hint: when running from a copy, also compare the executing tools dir (os.path.dirname(__file__)) against manifest covered[holdout tools]; or refuse to run outside the repo checkout
findings.why_it_matters: A session can be stamped as identity-verified while its code differs from what the manifest pinned.

findings.title: --manifest is required for gate/dev-tally/b3-aggregate/harness-verdicts, so the documented commands exit 2 and the active-manifest fallback never runs
findings.problem: _common(p, manifest_required=True) is the default, and only `list` passes False. The README documents `freeze_tally.py gate --gate <gate> --runs-root <R>` without --manifest; argparse rejects that and main() returns 2. _context() has `args.manifest or _active_manifest_path(series_dir)`, which is meant to pick the highest-N manifest, but it cannot be reached for these subcommands. It fails closed, but the documented release-gate invocation does not work.
findings.fix_hint: make --manifest optional for every subcommand (_context already resolves the active manifest), or fix the README commands
findings.why_it_matters: The gate command as documented always exits with a usage error.

findings.title: harness-verdicts prints a COMPLETE total without checking slot completeness when --roster is omitted, and counts extra slots
findings.intent_doc_match: freeze_tally docstring: 'there is no path that counts a run without both'; README: 'Gates are SLOT-based, never count-based'
findings.problem: The missing-slot check runs only inside `if roster is not None`. Without --roster, any set of eligible fix-harness runs with no duplicate is totalled as 'COMPLETE: N'. That includes runs whose slot is not mandatory (an unknown case or a B3 quiet diff), because by_slot is never filtered against GATE_SLOTS['workflow']. The output looks like a workflow tally even when 16 of the 18 slots are missing. The `gate` subcommand is the real gate, but this command presents itself as a filtered tally.
findings.current_code:
if roster is not None:
    ...
verdicts = [r.get("verdict") for rs in by_slot.values() for r in rs]
print("COMPLETE: %d" % verdicts.count("COMPLETE"))
findings.fix_hint: require --roster (or refuse to total without it) and list slots not in the mandatory set as extras instead of counting them
findings.why_it_matters: A partial or off-roster set of runs can read as a complete workflow total.

findings.title: Engineering record's candidate_guard is accepted on its prefix alone; the candidate it names is never compared
findings.intent_doc_match: README: candidate_guard is 'the freeze_check.py candidate-guard output line, beginning CANDIDATE OK'
findings.problem: _engineering_identity only checks guard.startswith('CANDIDATE OK'). The guard line has the form 'CANDIDATE OK candidate=<sha> head=<sha> ...', but its candidate= value is never checked against the record's candidate_sha. A record whose guard came from another candidate, or a copied or hand-written line, is still treated as candidate-bound. engineering_record_bound then trusts the record's own candidate_sha field.
findings.current_code: if not isinstance(guard, str) or not guard.startswith("CANDIDATE OK"):
findings.fix_hint: parse candidate=<40hex> from the guard line and require it to equal rec['candidate_sha']
findings.why_it_matters: An engineering slot can be filled by guard evidence that does not match the candidate it claims.

findings.title: Auto-memory move uses an unvalidated, hardcoded PARKDIR; an empty value moves the memory dir to /<repo>-written-...
findings.problem: PD comes from sed over a hardcoded ~/.b3/phase54-live-memory-park.env, with no check that the file exists or that PD is non-empty and a directory. If restore-memory already ran, or the env file is missing, PD is empty and the mv target becomes '/<CP>-written-during-live-...': the move fails on macOS or misplaces the evidence. mem_evidence in common.sh does validate PD. Hardcoding the phase54 filename instead of $MEMPARK_ENV also breaks the Phase-55 runbooks that inherit this driver.
findings.fix_hint: guard `test -n "$PD" && test -d "$PD"` (die otherwise) and read the park env path from the runbook rather than hardcoding phase54
findings.why_it_matters: Evidence of memory written during a measured session can be lost or misplaced.

findings.title: Finalize prose ignores review_archive.py's exit status; a failed archive is reported as done and flow continues
findings.problem: review_archive.py exits 1 when the move fails, for example when os.unlink(src) fails after os.link succeeded, or when no free name is found. The unstamped fence echoes 'archived aside' unconditionally after the call. A REVIEW.md that is still present then falls through to the stamped branch and is archived again under a phase name. The state archive step (line 60) has no stop-on-failure either, so the close-out can claim the state was archived while it is still live. pending: confirm the orchestrator does not check the exit code elsewhere.
findings.current_code:
python3 "$VC_ROOT/scripts/review_archive.py" unstamped --dir .turingmind
echo "An earlier REVIEW.md was written by ...; archived aside as REVIEW-unstamped-<date>.md ..."
findings.fix_hint: chain with `|| { echo ...; stop }` for all three review_archive.py calls
findings.why_it_matters: A half-done close-out (live state left behind, a double archive) goes unnoticed.

findings.title: Link-then-unlink leaves both source and archive when unlink fails, and exit 1 gives no hint the archive exists
findings.problem: If os.unlink(src) raises (permissions, an immutable flag), the archive hard link already exists. main() reports a failure, and a retry creates another '-N' archive of the same file. Nothing is lost, but the move is not atomic and the error path never removes the new link. pending: confirm unlink can fail in practice on the .turingmind dir.
findings.fix_hint: on unlink failure, remove the just-created target link (or report its path) before raising
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate archives and a misleading failure status.

findings.title: identity.json is written before exec; an exec failure leaves a stamped eligibility record for a run that never launched
findings.problem: write_identity runs before spawn(argv, ...). os.execvpe can raise OSError (claude not on PATH, ENOEXEC). That error is outside the try, so it propagates uncaught (main catches only KitError). The run dir keeps a valid identity.json with manifest_id, check_digest, candidate_sha and slot. freeze_policy.read_record treats it as an identity-ok holdout-eval record for (case_id, run-n). Only an external verdicts file then tells it apart from a real run.
findings.current_code:
write_identity(run_dir, result, case_id, run_name, session_id)
...
spawn(argv, session_env, run_dir)
findings.fix_hint: resolve the claude executable (shutil.which) before writing identity.json, and on exec failure rename the identity file or mark the run dir .failed-
findings.why_it_matters: A non-run can occupy a holdout slot as an eligible record.

findings.title: holdout-eval toml_absent check passes silently when no clone dir is given
findings.problem: For runner holdout-eval, clone_dir None returns [] (pass), where b3 returns CLONE_DIR_MISSING. The current launcher always passes clone_dir=run_dir, but any other caller of verify(runner='holdout-eval'), or a CLI `verify --runner holdout-eval` without --clone-dir, skips the .vibe-check.toml class with no problem line. That contradicts the module's 'no class can be skipped silently' contract. pending: confirm no other holdout-eval caller omits clone_dir.
findings.fix_hint: treat a missing clone dir as a problem for holdout-eval too
findings.why_it_matters: An identity class can pass without being checked.

findings.title: Seal-order proof accepts an empty retired_case_ids list
findings.intent_doc_match: README Retune: the owner's removal commit names the retired case ids
findings.problem: _proof_problems rejects an empty replacement list but not an empty retired list. The CLI defaults --retired to []. A retune proof can therefore be written and validated without naming which steered case was retired, so the 'case that guided the repair' is never recorded. pending: confirm a retune always retires at least one case.
findings.current_code: if not repl or set(repl) & set(retired):
findings.why_it_matters: The retune audit trail can omit the retired case.

findings.title: Non-dict enabledPlugins crashes generate with an uncaught AttributeError
findings.problem: user_level() calls (settings.get('enabledPlugins') or {}).items(). If enabledPlugins is a list or string, this raises AttributeError. verify() turns it into an 'observe failed' line, which is fail-closed. freeze_manifest.main catches only FreezeError, so generate exits with a traceback instead of a named refusal.
findings.current_code: for name, on in sorted((settings.get("enabledPlugins") or {}).items()):
findings.fix_hint: raise FreezeError when enabledPlugins is present but not a dict
findings.why_it_matters: A crash instead of a named refusal at manifest generation.

Checked and dropped: score.py run() pops needs_verification from fresh findings, but those dicts are copies made earlier in run() (the status scrub at ~L1680), so the caller's envelope is not changed.

fixharness: the launch_model passed to the identity check is read from the same manifest it is compared against, so that comparison is always equal. The real binding is the init-model check (_model_problems). Noted, not reported.

semgrep_replica: verdict needs every intended path in paths.scanned. Files in languages semgrep does not parse (shell, md, json) will probably keep the gate degraded. This matches the evidence commits (manual substitution for shell-parser gaps). It looks like a design choice, so it is not reported as a bug.
